cards.english: the bread / the apple (le / la)
cards.grammarNote:
Every French noun is masculine or feminine, and the article shows which:
**le** (masc.) / **la** (fem.); **un** / **une** for 'a'. → **le pain** (bread), **la pomme** (apple). Before a vowel, **le/la → l'**: **l'eau** (water).

table.title: French definite articles («the»)
table.note: Every noun has a gender — learn it with its article.

cards.english: I am a student. (subject pronoun required)
cards.grammarNote:
French always keeps the subject pronoun, and **être** (to be) is irregular:
**je suis** (I am), **tu es** (you are), **il/elle est** (he/she is), **nous sommes**, **vous êtes**, **ils/elles sont**.

table.title: être — to be
table.note: The subject pronoun is required in French.

cards.english: you (formal or plural → vous)
cards.grammarNote:
Two words for 'you': **tu** (informal, one person you know) · **vous** (formal, or more than one person):
**tu es** (a friend) vs **vous êtes** (a stranger, or a group). Using **tu** with a stranger can seem too familiar.

a.gloss: one friend, child, family — informal

b.gloss: a stranger/elder, or several people — formal & plural

cards.english: I don't understand. (ne … pas wraps the verb)
cards.grammarNote:
Negation wraps the verb in two parts: **ne** + verb + **pas**:
**je ne comprends pas** (I don't understand), **je ne sais pas** (I don't know). In casual speech the **ne** is often dropped: **je sais pas**.

produce.concept: Negation wraps the verb: ne + verb + pas
produce.task: say: I don't understand
produce.answer: je ne comprends pas
produce.gloss: ne … pas hug the verb. Before a vowel ne → n' : je n'ai pas.

cards.english: Do you speak French? (est-ce que)
cards.grammarNote:
Three ways to ask a yes/no question:
1) rising intonation — **Tu parles français ?**  2) add **est-ce que** in front — **Est-ce que tu parles français ?**  3) invert verb + pronoun — **Parles-tu français ?** (most formal).

produce.concept: Make a yes/no question with est-ce que + statement
produce.task: ask: do you speak French?
produce.answer: est-ce que tu parles français ?
produce.gloss: The word order after est-ce que doesn't change.

cards.english: some bread (du / de la / des)
cards.grammarNote:
For an unspecified quantity ('some'), French uses the partitive:
**du** (masc.) **du pain** (some bread), **de la** (fem.) **de la viande** (some meat), **de l'** before a vowel **de l'eau**, **des** (plural) **des pommes**.
cards.englishPhrase: I'm eating some bread and some cheese.
cards.phrase: Je mange du pain et du fromage.

cards.english: I would like a coffee. (je voudrais — polite)
cards.grammarNote:
**je voudrais** (I would like) is the polite way to order — softer than **je veux** (I want):
**je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît**. It's the conditional of **vouloir**.
cards.phrase: Je voudrais un thé, s'il vous plaît.

produce.concept: je voudrais = I would like (polite request)
produce.task: order: I would like a coffee
produce.answer: je voudrais un café
produce.gloss: Softer than je veux (I want).

cards.english: I like coffee. (j'aime + le/la)
cards.grammarNote:
With **aimer** (to like/love), use the **definite article** for things in general:
**j'aime le café** (I like coffee), **j'aime les pommes** (I like apples). Compare the partitive **du café** = 'some coffee' (a quantity).

a.gloss: like it in general → definite le/la

b.gloss: some of it → partitive du/de la

cards.english: It's delicious! (c'est + adjective)
cards.grammarNote:
**c'est** (it is / that is) + adjective gives a quick reaction:
**c'est délicieux** (it's delicious), **c'est bon** (it's good). The adjective stays masculine singular after **c'est**.

produce.task: say: it's delicious!
produce.answer: c'est délicieux
produce.gloss: Use c'est for a general 'it', with the masculine adjective form.

cards.english: There is a bank. (il y a)
cards.grammarNote:
**il y a** = there is / there are — one fixed phrase for both:
**il y a une banque** (there's a bank), **il y a deux musées** (there are two museums). Literally 'it there has'.
cards.phrase: Il y a un restaurant près d'ici ?

produce.concept: il y a = there is / there are (never changes)
produce.task: say: there is a bank
produce.answer: il y a une banque
produce.gloss: Same for plural: il y a deux banques.

cards.english: in the house (dans / sur / sous)
cards.grammarNote:
Common position words:
**dans** (in) **dans la maison**, **sur** (on) **sur la table**, **sous** (under) **sous le lit**, **devant** (in front of), **derrière** (behind), **à côté de** (next to).
cards.englishPhrase: The cat is on the table.
cards.phrase: Le chat est sur la table.

cards.english: to the / of the (à+le=au, de+le=du)
cards.grammarNote:
**à** and **de** contract before masculine **le** and plural **les**:
**à + le → au**, **à + les → aux**; **de + le → du**, **de + les → des**. → **au parc** (to the park), **la porte du café**. No change with **la** or **l'**.

table.title: Contractions with à and de
table.note: à la / de la don’t contract.

cards.english: I'm going to the park. (aller à + place)
cards.grammarNote:
**aller** (to go) + **à** for a destination; **à + le → au**:
**je vais au parc**, **je vais à la plage** (to the beach). **aller** is irregular: **je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont**.

produce.concept: aller à + place = to go to (à + le → au)
produce.task: say: I'm going to the park
produce.answer: je vais au parc
produce.gloss: à+le→au, à+les→aux; à la / à l' stay.

cards.english: I am a doctor. (no article: je suis médecin)
cards.grammarNote:
State a job with **être** and **no article**:
**je suis médecin** (I'm a doctor), **elle est ingénieure** (she's an engineer). Add an article only with a description: **c'est un bon médecin**.

a.gloss: just the job → no article

b.gloss: ✗ don't add un for a plain profession

cards.english: I like reading. (j'aime + infinitive)
cards.grammarNote:
To say you like doing something, use **aimer** + the infinitive:
**j'aime lire** (I like reading), **j'aime courir** (I like running). No 'to' or '-ing' — just the plain verb.

produce.task: say: I like reading
produce.answer: j'aime lire
produce.gloss: j'aime + the infinitive. j'aime courir = I like running.

cards.english: I work as a nurse. (travailler comme / dans / chez)
cards.grammarNote:
**travailler comme** = to work as; **travailler dans** = in (a field/place); **travailler chez** = at (a company):
**je travaille comme infirmier**, **dans un hôpital**, **chez Google**.

table.title: Talking about your job
table.note: comme = as; chez = at a company/person; dans = in a place.

cards.english: I go swimming. (faire de la natation)
cards.grammarNote:
Many sports and hobbies use **faire de** + activity:
**je fais de la natation** (I swim), **je fais du vélo** (I cycle). **faire** is irregular: **je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font**.
cards.englishPhrase: I go hiking on the weekend.
cards.phrase: Je fais de la randonnée le week-end.

produce.concept: faire de + activity = to do / play (sports, hobbies)
produce.task: say: I go swimming
produce.answer: je fais de la natation
produce.gloss: de+le→du (faire du sport), de la, de l'.

cards.english: I am happy. (adjective agrees: heureux / heureuse)
cards.grammarNote:
Feelings use **être** + an adjective that agrees with you:
**je suis heureux** (a man) / **je suis heureuse** (a woman). Add **-e** for feminine, **-s** for plural: **ils sont contents**.

cloze.prompt: She is happy. (adjective agrees)

cards.english: I am afraid. (avoir peur — 'have fear')
cards.grammarNote:
Some feelings use **avoir** (to have), not **être**:
**j'ai peur** (I'm afraid), **j'ai honte** (I'm ashamed). Also physical states: **j'ai faim** (hungry), **j'ai froid** (cold).

a.gloss: «I have fear» — a few use avoir + noun (faim, soif, peur)

b.gloss: «I am sad» — most use être + adjective

cards.english: She is nervous. (adjective agrees → nerveuse)
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives change to match gender and number:
**il est nerveux** / **elle est nerveuse** / **ils sont nerveux** / **elles sont nerveuses**. Many **-eux** adjectives become **-euse** in the feminine.

cloze.prompt: She is nervous. (adjective agrees → feminine)

cards.english: I feel tired. (je me sens — reflexive)
cards.grammarNote:
**se sentir** (to feel) is reflexive — the pronoun matches the subject:
**je me sens** (I feel), **tu te sens**, **il se sent**. In **je me sens fatigué(e)** the adjective still agrees with you.
cards.englishPhrase: How do you feel? — I feel good.
cards.phrase: Comment tu te sens ? — Je me sens bien.

produce.task: say: I feel tired
produce.answer: je me sens fatigué
produce.gloss: je me sens, tu te sens, il se sent. Agrees: fatiguée (f).

cards.english: I wash my hands. (je me lave les mains)
cards.grammarNote:
With body parts and a reflexive verb, French uses **the** (le/la/les), not 'my':
**je me lave les mains** (I wash my hands), **il se brosse les dents** (he brushes his teeth). The reflexive pronoun already shows whose.

cloze.prompt: I wash my hands. (definite article, not «mes»)

cards.english: My head hurts. (avoir mal à)
cards.grammarNote:
To say something hurts, use **avoir mal à** + body part (with contraction **à + le → au**):
**j'ai mal à la tête** (headache), **j'ai mal au dos** (backache), **j'ai mal aux pieds** (my feet hurt).

cloze.prompt: My back hurts. (à + le → ?)

cards.english: my hand / my eyes (ma / mes)
cards.grammarNote:
Possessives agree with the noun (not the owner):
**mon** (masc.) / **ma** (fem.) / **mes** (plural) → **mon bras**, **ma main**, **mes yeux**. Before a vowel use **mon** even for feminine: **mon amie**.

cards.english: She has blue eyes. (avoir + les + adjective)
cards.grammarNote:
Describe features with **avoir** + **les** + body part + adjective (which agrees):
**elle a les yeux bleus** (she has blue eyes), **il a les cheveux courts** (he has short hair).

produce.concept: Describe the body with avoir + article + adjective
produce.task: say: she has blue eyes
produce.answer: elle a les yeux bleus
produce.gloss: Literally 'she has the eyes blue'; the adjective follows & agrees.

cards.english: -er verbs in the present (parler model)
cards.grammarNote:
Most **-er** verbs follow this pattern: drop **-er**, add **-e / -es / -e / -ons / -ez / -ent**.
Silent endings: the **-e, -es, -ent** endings are all pronounced the same.

table.title: parler — to speak (present)
table.note: The -e, -es, -ent endings are silent — parle/parles/parlent all sound alike.

cards.english: -ir verbs in the present (finir model)
cards.grammarNote:
Regular **-ir** verbs: drop **-ir**, add **-is / -is / -it / -issons / -issez / -issent**.
Note the **-iss-** that appears in the plural forms.

table.title: finir — to finish (present)
table.note: The -iss- appears in the plural: finissons, finissez, finissent.

cards.english: -re verbs in the present (vendre model)
cards.grammarNote:
Regular **-re** verbs: drop **-re**, add **-s / -s / — / -ons / -ez / -ent**.
The **il/elle** form has NO ending — just the stem: **il vend**.
cards.englishPhrase: They sell bread at the market.
cards.phrase: Ils vendent du pain au marché.

table.title: vendre — to sell (present)
table.note: The il/elle form has no ending — just the bare stem: il vend.

cards.english: être (to be) — fully irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**être** is completely irregular — memorise every form:
**je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont**.

table.title: être — to be (present)
table.note: Fully irregular — no pattern to follow. Learn all six forms.

cards.english: avoir (to have) — irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**avoir** is irregular: **j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont**.
Used for age, hunger, thirst — and as the auxiliary in passé composé.
cards.phrase: Est-ce que vous avez la carte ?

table.title: avoir — to have (present)
table.note: Critical irregular: j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont.

cards.english: aller (to go) — irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**aller** is irregular: **je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont**.
Also used to form the near future: **je vais manger** (I'm going to eat).
cards.englishPhrase: Are you going to the museum?

table.title: aller — to go (present)
table.note: aller is the base for near future: je vais + infinitive.

cards.english: faire (to do / make) — irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**faire** is irregular: **je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font**.
Note: **vous faites** is irregular — not *vous faisez*.

table.title: faire — to do / make (present)
table.note: vous faites is irregular — not faisez.

cards.english: near future: aller + infinitive
cards.grammarNote:
The near future (futur proche) is formed with **aller** (present) + **infinitive**:
**je vais manger** (I'm going to eat), **elle va partir** (she's going to leave).
cards.englishPhrase: We are going to eat at the restaurant.

produce.task: say: I am going to eat / she is going to leave
produce.answer: je vais manger / elle va partir
produce.gloss: aller present tense + the infinitive of any verb.

cards.english: We eat at the restaurant. (nous form of manger)
cards.grammarNote:
Verbs ending in **-ger** add an **e** before **-ons** to preserve the soft g sound:
**manger → nous mangeons** (not *nous mangons*).
cards.phrase: Nous mangeons du pain au petit-déjeuner.

cloze.prompt: We eat breakfast. (-ger verb: keep the soft g)

cards.english: She is leaving now. (partir — irregular -ir verb)
cards.grammarNote:
Some **-ir** verbs are irregular — **partir** does NOT follow the finir pattern:
**je pars, tu pars, il part, nous partons, vous partez, ils partent**. Drop the consonant before the singular endings.

cloze.prompt: She leaves. (partir — irregular -ir, il/elle form)

cards.english: present vs. near future — what's the difference?
cards.grammarNote:
Use the **present** for habitual or current actions; use **aller + infinitive** for what's about to happen:
**je mange** (I eat / I am eating) vs. **je vais manger** (I'm going to eat).
cards.englishPhrase: I eat at the restaurant. vs. I'm going to eat at the restaurant.
cards.phrase: Je mange au restaurant. / Je vais manger au restaurant.

a.gloss: I eat / I am eating — habit or current action

b.gloss: I am going to eat — imminent or planned action

cards.english: vouloir (to want) — irregular present
cards.grammarNote:
**vouloir** is irregular: **je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent**.
The **-eul-** stem in singular vs. **-oul-** in plural is a typical boot-verb alternation.

table.title: vouloir — to want (present)
table.note: Boot verb: veux/veut/veulent in the singular & ils, voulons/voulez in nous/vous.

cards.english: pouvoir (to be able to) — irregular present
cards.grammarNote:
**pouvoir** is irregular: **je peux, tu peux, il peut, nous pouvons, vous pouvez, ils peuvent**.
Like vouloir, it has a boot pattern.

table.title: pouvoir — to be able to (present)
table.note: je peux / tu peux / il peut (singular) — nous pouvons / vous pouvez (plural).

cards.english: Do you (formal) speak French? (vous form of parler)
cards.grammarNote:
The **vous** form of **-er** verbs ends in **-ez**: **parlez, mangez, regardez**.
Inversion question: **parlez-vous ?** — verb before pronoun with a hyphen.

cloze.prompt: Do you (formal) speak French? (inversion)

cards.english: avoir for age — how old are you?
cards.grammarNote:
French uses **avoir** (not être) for age:
**j'ai vingt ans** (I am twenty), **il a trente ans** (he is thirty). Never *je suis vingt ans*.

cloze.prompt: I am twenty years old. (avoir for age, not être)

cards.english: passé composé with avoir (basic structure)
cards.grammarNote:
The **passé composé** = **avoir** (present) + **past participle**.
For most verbs use **avoir**: **j'ai mangé** (I ate), **tu as fini** (you finished), **il a vendu** (he sold).

table.title: passé composé — avoir + participle
table.note: The participle (mangé) stays the same with avoir — no agreement.

cards.english: past participles of -er, -ir, -re verbs
cards.grammarNote:
Form the past participle by the verb type:
**-er → -é** (parler → **parlé**); **-ir → -i** (finir → **fini**); **-re → -u** (vendre → **vendu**).

table.title: Past participle formation
table.note: These three rules cover most regular verbs.

cards.english: passé composé with être (motion & state verbs)
cards.grammarNote:
A set of verbs (mainly motion/state) use **être** instead of **avoir**: **aller, venir, partir, rester, arriver, entrer, sortir, naître, mourir** and their compounds.
**je suis allé(e)** (I went) — the participle agrees with the subject.

table.title: être verbs — DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP
table.note: Participle agrees with subject: elle est allEE, ils sont allES.

cards.english: participle agreement with être verbs
cards.word: elle est partie / ils sont partis
cards.grammarNote:
With **être** verbs, the past participle agrees like an adjective with the subject:
**il est parti** (masc. sing.) / **elle est partie** (fem. sing.) / **ils sont partis** / **elles sont parties**.

cloze.prompt: She left. (être + agreement → feminine form)

cards.english: irregular past participles
cards.grammarNote:
Key irregular past participles to memorise:
**avoir → eu**, **être → été**, **faire → fait**, **voir → vu**, **pouvoir → pu**, **vouloir → voulu**, **venir → venu**, **prendre → pris**.

table.title: Irregular past participles
table.note: These five are the most common — learn them first.

cards.english: negation in the passé composé
cards.grammarNote:
In the passé composé, **ne … pas** wraps the **auxiliary** (avoir/être), not the participle:
**je n'ai pas mangé** (I didn't eat), **il n'est pas parti** (he didn't leave).
cards.phrase: Je n'ai pas mangé le petit-déjeuner.

produce.task: say: I didn't eat / she didn't leave
produce.answer: je n'ai pas mangé / elle n'est pas partie
produce.gloss: ne…pas sandwiches the auxiliary verb: je n'ai pas mangé.

cards.english: avoir or être? (choosing the auxiliary)
cards.grammarNote:
Choose **avoir** for most verbs; choose **être** for the DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP motion/state verbs and all reflexives.
**j'ai mangé** (ate — avoir); **je suis allé** (went — être).
cards.englishPhrase: I ate at the restaurant. / I went to the restaurant.
cards.phrase: J'ai mangé au restaurant. / Je suis allé au restaurant.

contrast.prompt: manger vs aller — avoir or être?

a.gloss: manger → avoir (most verbs take avoir)

b.gloss: aller → être (motion verb, participle agrees)

cards.english: You finished the meal. (tu form of finir in passé composé)
cards.grammarNote:
**finir** (to finish) in passé composé: **avoir** + **fini** (the -ir participle).
**tu as fini le repas** — the participle does not change with avoir.

cloze.prompt: You finished the meal. (finir → passé composé)

cards.english: They came to the restaurant. (venir → être auxiliary)
cards.grammarNote:
**venir** uses **être** as auxiliary; participle is **venu**:
**il est venu / elle est venue / ils sont venus / elles sont venues**.

cloze.prompt: They (masc.) came. (venir → être, agreement)

cards.english: What did you do? (faire in passé composé)
cards.grammarNote:
**faire → fait** (irregular participle): **j'ai fait, tu as fait, il a fait**.
**Qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?** = what did you do?
cards.phrase: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait aujourd'hui ?

produce.task: say: I made a salad / what did you do?
produce.answer: j'ai fait une salade / qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?
produce.gloss: faire → fait. avoir auxiliary. Invariable participle.

cards.english: She left early. (partir — être auxiliary)
cards.grammarNote:
**partir** (to leave) uses **être** and its participle is **parti(e)**:
**je suis parti(e), tu es parti(e), il est parti, elle est partie, nous sommes parti(e)s, vous êtes parti(e)s, ils sont partis, elles sont parties**.

produce.concept: partir → parti(e) with être; participle agrees
produce.task: say: he left / she left
produce.answer: il est parti / elle est partie
produce.gloss: être auxiliary: il est parti (no -e), elle est partie (+e).

cards.english: We arrived at the station. (arriver — être)
cards.grammarNote:
**arriver** uses **être**: participle **arrivé(e)(s)**.
**nous sommes arrivés** (masc./mixed group) / **nous sommes arrivées** (all-female).
cards.phrase: Nous sommes arrivés à la gare.

cloze.prompt: We (masc./mixed) arrived at the station.

cards.english: I saw the museum. (voir — irregular participle vu)
cards.grammarNote:
**voir** (to see) has the irregular participle **vu**:
**j'ai vu le musée** (I saw the museum). Uses **avoir** — no agreement.

cloze.prompt: I saw the museum. (voir → irregular participle)

cards.english: reflexive verbs in passé composé — always use être
cards.grammarNote:
All reflexive verbs use **être** in the passé composé:
**je me suis senti(e)** (I felt), **elle s'est sentie** (she felt). The reflexive pronoun stays before the auxiliary.

contrast.prompt: Reflexive in passé composé — avoir or être?

a.gloss: reflexive → always être: me suis senti (I felt)

b.gloss: non-reflexive → avoir (I ate)

cards.english: imparfait — how to form it
cards.grammarNote:
The **imparfait** is formed from the **nous present stem** + endings: **-ais / -ais / -ait / -ions / -iez / -aient**.
Take the nous form, drop **-ons**, add the endings: mang**ons** → mang + **ais**.

table.title: manger — imparfait
table.note: Stem = nous present minus -ons (mang-). Only être is irregular: étais, étais, était...

cards.english: être in the imparfait — the only irregular stem
cards.grammarNote:
Only **être** has an irregular imparfait stem: **ét-** (not *somm-*).
**j'étais, tu étais, il était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils étaient** (I was, you were, etc.).

table.title: être — imparfait (irregular stem: ét-)
table.note: Only irregular stem in the imparfait. All other verbs use the nous-present stem.

cards.english: imparfait for habits vs. passé composé for events
cards.grammarNote:
**Imparfait** = ongoing background, habits, repeated past actions (used to, was -ing).
**Passé composé** = completed event, one-time action, specific moment.
cards.englishPhrase: I used to eat here. vs. I ate here yesterday.
cards.phrase: Je mangeais ici. / J'ai mangé ici hier.

a.gloss: imparfait — I used to eat here (habit/repeated)

b.gloss: passé composé — I ate here yesterday (single completed event)

cards.english: imparfait = background; passé composé = foreground
cards.grammarNote:
Imparfait sets the **background scene**; passé composé interrupts with an **event**:
**Il pleuvait** (it was raining — background) **quand je suis arrivé** (when I arrived — event).
cards.englishPhrase: It was raining when I arrived.
cards.phrase: Il pleuvait quand je suis arrivé.

produce.task: combine: it was raining (imp.) + I arrived (PC)
produce.answer: il pleuvait quand je suis arrivé
produce.gloss: pleuvait = imparfait background; suis arrivé = passé composé event.

cards.english: imparfait for descriptions and mental states
cards.grammarNote:
Use the **imparfait** for past states, feelings, descriptions, and mental states:
**j'étais fatigué** (I was tired), **il faisait beau** (the weather was nice), **elle voulait partir** (she wanted to leave).
cards.englishPhrase: I was tired and I wanted to leave.
cards.phrase: J'étais fatigué et je voulais partir.

cloze.prompt: I was tired. (past state → imparfait)

cards.english: We used to eat at the restaurant. (imparfait — habit)
cards.grammarNote:
Repeated/habitual past action → **imparfait**:
**nous mangions au restaurant** (we used to eat / we would eat at the restaurant).
cards.englishPhrase: We used to eat at the restaurant every day.
cards.phrase: Nous mangions au restaurant tous les jours.

cloze.prompt: We used to eat at the restaurant. (habit → imparfait)

cards.english: They spoke to the doctor. (single event → passé composé)
cards.grammarNote:
A specific, completed past event → **passé composé**:
**ils ont parlé au médecin** (they spoke to the doctor — it happened once).

cloze.prompt: They spoke to the doctor. (single event → passé composé)

cards.english: avoir in the imparfait
cards.grammarNote:
**avoir** imparfait: stem **av-** (from **av**ons) + endings:
**j'avais, tu avais, il avait, nous avions, vous aviez, ils avaient**.

table.title: avoir — imparfait
table.note: Stem: av- (from avons). Regular endings apply.

cards.english: time triggers — which tense do they signal?
cards.grammarNote:
Certain time words signal the tense:
**Imparfait**: toujours (always), souvent (often), chaque jour (every day), d'habitude (usually).
**Passé composé**: hier (yesterday), soudain (suddenly), une fois (once).
cards.englishPhrase: I always ate at the restaurant. vs. Yesterday I ate here.
cards.phrase: Je mangeais toujours au restaurant. / Hier, j'ai mangé ici.

table.title: Time-word triggers
table.note: These aren't absolute rules, but they're strong signals.

cards.english: vouloir: wanted (imp.) vs. tried/decided (PC)
cards.word: il voulait partir / il a voulu partir
cards.grammarNote:
Some verbs shift meaning between the two tenses:
**il voulait partir** (he wanted to leave — ongoing desire) vs. **il a voulu partir** (he tried/decided to leave — specific moment).
cards.englishPhrase: He wanted to leave. vs. He tried to leave.
cards.phrase: Il voulait partir. / Il a voulu partir.

a.gloss: imparfait — ongoing wish/state (he wanted to leave)

b.gloss: passé composé — decided/attempted in that moment

cards.english: mix: background (imparfait) + event (passé composé)
cards.word: j'étais au restaurant quand il est arrivé
cards.grammarNote:
When combining the two tenses, the **imparfait** gives the backdrop and the **passé composé** gives the action that happened:
**j'étais au restaurant** (background) **quand il est arrivé** (event).
cards.englishPhrase: I was at the restaurant when he arrived.
cards.phrase: J'étais au restaurant quand il est arrivé.

produce.task: say: I was at the restaurant when he arrived
produce.answer: j'étais au restaurant quand il est arrivé
produce.gloss: étais = imparfait (state); est arrivé = passé composé (event).

cards.english: il faisait beau — weather in the imparfait
cards.grammarNote:
Weather descriptions in the past always use the **imparfait**:
**il faisait beau** (the weather was nice), **il faisait chaud** (it was hot), **il faisait froid** (it was cold).

cloze.prompt: The weather was nice. (past description → imparfait)

cards.english: parler in the imparfait — all forms
cards.grammarNote:
**parler** imparfait: stem **parl-** + endings **-ais/-ais/-ait/-ions/-iez/-aient**.
**je parlais, tu parlais, il parlait, nous parlions, vous parliez, ils parlaient**.
cards.englishPhrase: I was speaking to the doctor.

produce.task: give imparfait: je / nous / ils for parler
produce.answer: je parlais / nous parlions / ils parlaient
produce.gloss: stem parl- + ais / ions / aient.

cards.english: finir in the imparfait
cards.grammarNote:
**finir** imparfait: stem from **finissons** → **finiss-** + endings.
**je finissais, tu finissais, il finissait, nous finissions, vous finissiez, ils finissaient**.

cloze.prompt: She was finishing the meal. (finir → imparfait stem: finiss-)

cards.english: future tense — infinitive + endings
cards.grammarNote:
The **futur simple** = infinitive + endings: **-ai / -as / -a / -ons / -ez / -ont**.
For **-re** verbs, drop the final **e** first: vendre → vendr + ai.
**je mangerai** (I will eat), **tu finiras** (you will finish), **il vendra** (he will sell).
cards.englishPhrase: I will eat at the restaurant.

table.title: manger — futur simple
table.note: Infinitive + ending. -re verbs drop final -e: vendre → vendrai.

cards.english: irregular future stems — être, avoir, aller, faire, vouloir
cards.grammarNote:
These verbs have **irregular future stems** (the endings are still regular):
**être → ser-** (serai), **avoir → aur-** (aurai), **aller → ir-** (irai), **faire → fer-** (ferai), **vouloir → voudr-** (voudrai), **pouvoir → pourr-** (pourrai).
cards.englishPhrase: I will be at the restaurant.

table.title: Irregular future stems
table.note: Stems are irregular; endings (-ai/-as/-a/-ons/-ez/-ont) are always the same.

cards.english: conditional — infinitive + imparfait endings
cards.grammarNote:
The **conditionnel** = infinitive + imparfait endings: **-ais / -ais / -ait / -ions / -iez / -aient**.
Same stem as the futur (incl. irregular stems): **je serais** (I would be), **j'aurais** (I would have).
cards.englishPhrase: I would eat at the restaurant.

table.title: manger — conditionnel
table.note: Same stem as futur + imparfait endings. je mangeRAIS (note the -ais ending).

cards.english: future vs. conditional — will vs. would
cards.grammarNote:
**Futur simple** = will (certainty/plan): **je mangerai** (I will eat).
**Conditionnel** = would (hypothetical/polite): **je mangerais** (I would eat).
The only difference: **-ai** (fut.) vs. **-ais** (cond.) in the je form — listen carefully.
cards.englishPhrase: I will eat there. vs. I would eat there.
cards.phrase: Je mangerai là-bas. / Je mangerais là-bas.

a.gloss: futur — I will eat (definite plan)

b.gloss: conditionnel — I would eat (hypothetical)

cards.english: We will go to the museum. (aller — irregular future stem: ir-)
cards.grammarNote:
**aller** future stem: **ir-** (not all-)
**j'irai, tu iras, il ira, nous irons, vous irez, ils iront**.
cards.englishPhrase: We will go to the museum.

cloze.prompt: We will go to the museum. (aller → irregular future)

cards.english: It would be good. (être — conditional: serait)
cards.grammarNote:
**être** conditional stem: **ser-** + endings.
**je serais, tu serais, il serait, nous serions, vous seriez, ils seraient**.
cards.englishPhrase: It would be good to eat here.
cards.phrase: Ce serait bien de manger ici.

cloze.prompt: It would be good. (être → conditional: ser-)

cards.english: je voudrais — the polite conditional
cards.grammarNote:
**je voudrais** (I would like) is the conditional of **vouloir** — used for polite requests:
**je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît** (I'd like a coffee, please). Softer than **je veux**.
cards.englishPhrase: I would like a tea, please.
cards.phrase: Je voudrais un thé, s'il vous plaît.

produce.task: order politely: a coffee / a sandwich
produce.answer: je voudrais un café / je voudrais un sandwich
produce.gloss: vouloir → voudr- + ais = voudrais. More polite than je veux.

cards.english: si + present → future (real condition)
cards.word: si tu manges, tu iras mieux
cards.grammarNote:
In a real conditional: **si + present → futur simple**:
**si tu manges**, tu iras mieux (if you eat, you will feel better). Never use the future in the si-clause itself.
cards.englishPhrase: If you eat, you will feel better.
cards.phrase: Si tu manges, tu iras mieux.

produce.task: complete: if you eat (present) + you will feel better (futur)
produce.answer: si tu manges, tu iras mieux
produce.gloss: si-clause: present (manges). Result: futur (iras). Never futur in si-clause.

cards.english: si + imparfait → conditional (hypothetical)
cards.word: si j'avais de l'argent, je voyagerais
cards.grammarNote:
Hypothetical/unreal conditions: **si + imparfait → conditionnel**:
**si j'avais de l'argent, je voyagerais** (if I had money, I would travel). Compare: real condition uses si + present + futur.
cards.englishPhrase: If I had more time, I would eat here.
cards.phrase: Si j'avais plus de temps, je mangerais ici.

a.term: si tu manges, tu iras mieux
a.gloss: real: si + present → futur (likely to happen)

b.term: si tu mangeais mieux, tu irais mieux
b.gloss: hypothetical: si + imparfait → conditionnel (unlikely/imagined)

cards.english: What will you do? (faire — irregular future stem: fer-)
cards.grammarNote:
**faire** future stem: **fer-**
**je ferai, tu feras, il fera, nous ferons, vous ferez, ils feront**.

cloze.prompt: What will you (formal) do? (faire → irregular future)

cards.english: avoir in the future — all forms
cards.grammarNote:
**avoir** future stem: **aur-**
**j'aurai, tu auras, il aura, nous aurons, vous aurez, ils auront**.
cards.englishPhrase: You will have a good meal.

produce.task: give future: j' / tu / nous for avoir
produce.answer: j'aurai / tu auras / nous aurons
produce.gloss: Irregular stem aur- + standard endings: -ai, -as, -ons.

cards.english: parler in the conditional
cards.grammarNote:
**parler** conditional: stem **parler-** (infinitive, keep the -r) + imparfait endings.
**je parlerais, tu parlerais, il parlerait, nous parlerions, vous parleriez, ils parleraient**.
cards.englishPhrase: I would speak French in Paris.

produce.task: give conditional: je / il / nous for parler
produce.answer: je parlerais / il parlerait / nous parlerions
produce.gloss: Stem = infinitive (parler). Add imparfait endings: -ais, -ait, -ions.

cards.english: Could you help me? (pouvoir — conditional: pourrait)
cards.grammarNote:
**pouvoir** conditional stem: **pourr-** + endings.
**je pourrais, tu pourrais, il pourrait, nous pourrions, vous pourriez, ils pourraient**.
**Pourriez-vous m'aider ?** = could you help me? (very polite).

cloze.prompt: Could you (formal) help me? (pouvoir → conditional stem: pourr-)

cards.english: venir in the future — irregular stem
cards.grammarNote:
**venir** future stem: **viendr-**
**je viendrai, tu viendras, il viendra, nous viendrons, vous viendrez, ils viendront**.
cards.englishPhrase: I will come to the restaurant.

cloze.prompt: I will come to the restaurant. (venir → irregular future: viendr-)

cards.english: direct object pronouns (le / la / les / me / te / nous / vous)
cards.grammarNote:
Direct object pronouns replace the direct object (who/what receives the action directly):
**me** (me), **te** (you), **le** (him/it masc.), **la** (her/it fem.), **nous** (us), **vous** (you pl.), **les** (them).

table.title: Direct object pronouns
table.note: Place before the conjugated verb: je le mange, tu la vois.

cards.english: indirect object pronouns (lui / leur)
cards.grammarNote:
Indirect object pronouns replace **à + person** (to him, to her, to them):
**lui** = to him / to her (singular); **leur** = to them (plural).
For 1st/2nd person: **me** (to me), **te** (to you), **nous** (to us), **vous** (to you pl.).

table.title: Indirect object pronouns (à + person)
table.note: lui replaces à + one person; leur replaces à + plural persons.

cards.english: y — replaces à + place (or à + non-person thing)
cards.grammarNote:
**y** replaces **à** + place (or à + thing, not a person):
**tu vas au musée ? → tu y vas ?** (are you going there?). **y** goes before the verb.
cards.englishPhrase: Are you going to the restaurant? Yes, I'm going there.
cards.phrase: Tu vas au restaurant ? — Oui, j'y vais.

produce.concept: y replaces à + place / à + non-person thing
produce.task: replace: je vais au parc → ?
produce.answer: j'y vais
produce.gloss: y = there/it (à+place). Place before verb: j'y vais, il y va.

cards.english: en — replaces de + noun (or partitive object)
cards.grammarNote:
**en** replaces **de + noun** or a partitive object (some of it, of them):
**tu manges du pain ? → tu en manges ?** (do you eat some [of it]?). **en** goes before the verb.
cards.englishPhrase: Do you eat some bread? Yes, I eat some.
cards.phrase: Tu manges du pain ? — Oui, j'en mange.

produce.concept: en replaces de + noun / partitive (some/of it)
produce.task: replace: je mange du pain → ?
produce.answer: j'en mange
produce.gloss: en = some / of it. Before verb: j'en mange. Also: il y en a (there is some).

cards.english: placement — object pronouns go before the conjugated verb
cards.word: je le mange / je l'ai mangé
cards.grammarNote:
Object pronouns go **directly before the conjugated verb** (or before the infinitive if there's one):
**je le mange** (I eat it — present), **je l'ai mangé** (I ate it — passé composé), **je veux le manger** (I want to eat it — infinitive).

table.title: Pronoun placement
table.note: With infinitive: pronoun goes before the infinitive, not the main verb.

cards.english: I see him at the restaurant. (le = direct object)
cards.grammarNote:
Replace the direct object with **le** (masc. sing.) before the verb:
**je vois le médecin → je le vois**.
cards.englishPhrase: I see him at the restaurant.

cloze.prompt: I see him. (direct object pronoun, masc. sing.)

cards.english: I speak to her. (lui = indirect object)
cards.grammarNote:
Replace **à + person** with **lui** (sing.) or **leur** (pl.) before the verb:
**je parle à la médecin → je lui parle** (I speak to her).

cloze.prompt: I speak to her. (indirect object: à + person → ?)

cards.english: le (direct) vs. lui (indirect) — what's the difference?
cards.word: je le vois / je lui parle
cards.grammarNote:
**le/la** = direct object (no preposition in French): **je le vois** (I see him).
**lui** = indirect object (replaces à + person): **je lui parle** (I speak to him).
Key: does the verb take a direct object or **parler à / donner à** etc.?
cards.englishPhrase: I see him. / I speak to him.
cards.phrase: Je le vois. / Je lui parle.

a.gloss: le = direct object (voir qqn — no à)

b.gloss: lui = indirect object (parler à qqn — via à)

cards.english: double pronouns — order before the verb
cards.grammarNote:
When two pronouns appear, the order is: **me/te/nous/vous → le/la/les → lui/leur → y → en**.
**je le lui donne** (I give it to him) — direct (le) before indirect (lui).
Exception: with me/te/nous/vous, those come first: **je vous le donne** (I give it to you).

table.title: Double-pronoun order
table.note: Example: je le lui donne (le before lui); je vous le donne (vous before le).

cards.english: I go there every day. (y = there)
cards.grammarNote:
**y** replaces **à / au / dans / en / sur + place**:
**je vais au parc → j'y vais** (I go there). Placed before the verb.

cloze.prompt: I go there every day. (replace au parc with y)

cards.english: I want some. (en replaces du / de la / des + noun)
cards.grammarNote:
**en** replaces a partitive or de + noun:
**tu veux du pain ? → tu en veux ?** (do you want some?). In the answer: **j'en veux** (I want some).
cards.englishPhrase: Do you want some bread? Yes, I want some.
cards.phrase: Tu veux du pain ? — Oui, j'en veux.

cloze.prompt: I want some bread → I want some. (en for partitive)

cards.english: negation with object pronouns — ne … pas around verb+pronoun
cards.grammarNote:
In negation, **ne … pas** wraps the **pronoun + verb** unit:
**je ne le mange pas** (I don't eat it), **je ne lui parle pas** (I don't speak to him).

produce.task: negate: je le mange / je lui parle
produce.answer: je ne le mange pas / je ne lui parle pas
produce.gloss: ne comes before the pronoun; pas comes after the verb.

cards.english: direct object before avoir in passé composé → participle agrees
cards.grammarNote:
When a **direct object pronoun** precedes **avoir** in the passé composé, the participle agrees with it:
**je l'ai mangée** (fem., so mangéE) — **la** replaces **la salade**.

cloze.prompt: The salad — I ate it. (la → direct object, fem. → participle agrees)

cards.english: I speak to them. (leur = indirect, plural)
cards.grammarNote:
**leur** = indirect object pronoun for plural persons (replaces **à** + plural group):
**je parle aux médecins → je leur parle** (I speak to them).

produce.task: replace: je parle aux médecins / je donne le pain aux enfants
produce.answer: je leur parle / je le leur donne
produce.gloss: leur for indirect plural. Double pronoun: le (direct) before leur (indirect).

cards.english: subjunctive — how to form it
cards.grammarNote:
The **subjonctif** is formed from the **ils/elles present stem** + endings: **-e / -es / -e / -ions / -iez / -ent**.
For **nous/vous**, use the imparfait forms (which happen to match): **que nous mangions, que vous mangiez**.

table.title: manger — subjonctif présent
table.note: Stem = ils/elles present (mang-). Nous/vous use imparfait-shaped endings.

cards.english: être and avoir in the subjunctive — irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**être** subjunctive: **que je sois, que tu sois, qu'il soit, que nous soyons, que vous soyez, qu'ils soient**.
**avoir** subjunctive: **que j'aie, que tu aies, qu'il ait, que nous ayons, que vous ayez, qu'ils aient**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to be here.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu sois ici.

table.title: être / avoir — subjonctif (irregular)
table.note: Both are fully irregular — learn them as vocabulary.

cards.english: vouloir que + subjunctive
cards.grammarNote:
**vouloir que** (to want that) triggers the subjunctive — when the subject of the main clause differs from the subject of the second clause:
**je veux que tu manges** (I want you to eat). If same subject, use infinitive: **je veux manger**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to eat the bread.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu manges le pain.

a.gloss: same subject → infinitive (I want to eat)

b.gloss: different subject → subjunctive (I want you to eat)

cards.english: il faut que + subjunctive (it is necessary that)
cards.grammarNote:
**il faut que** (it is necessary that / you must) always triggers the subjunctive:
**il faut que tu manges** (you must eat), **il faut que nous partions** (we need to leave).
Alternate: **il faut + infinitive** when no subject: **il faut manger** (one must eat).

produce.concept: il faut que + subjunctive (necessity, specific subject)
produce.task: say: you must eat / we need to leave
produce.answer: il faut que tu manges / il faut que nous partions
produce.gloss: il faut que always triggers subjunctive. Without subject: il faut manger.

cards.english: bien que + subjunctive (although)
cards.grammarNote:
**bien que** (although) always requires the subjunctive:
**bien qu'il soit fatigué** (although he is tired), **bien que nous soyons au restaurant** (although we are at the restaurant).
cards.englishPhrase: Although he is tired, he is working.
cards.phrase: Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il travaille.

cloze.prompt: Although he is tired... (bien que → subjunctive of être)

cards.english: pour que + subjunctive (so that)
cards.grammarNote:
**pour que** (so that / in order that) triggers the subjunctive:
**je prépare le repas pour que tu manges** (I prepare the meal so that you eat). If same subject, use **pour + infinitive**: **je mange pour vivre** (I eat to live).
cards.englishPhrase: I prepare the meal so that you can eat.
cards.phrase: Je prépare le repas pour que tu manges.

produce.task: say: I prepare the meal so that you eat
produce.answer: je prépare le repas pour que tu manges
produce.gloss: pour que + subjunctive; same subject → pour + infinitive.

cards.english: avant que + subjunctive (before)
cards.grammarNote:
**avant que** (before) triggers the subjunctive:
**avant que tu partes** (before you leave), **avant que nous mangions** (before we eat).

cloze.prompt: Eat before you leave. (avant que → subjunctive of partir)

cards.english: aller in the subjunctive — irregular
cards.grammarNote:
**aller** has an irregular subjunctive:
**que j'aille, que tu ailles, qu'il aille, que nous allions, que vous alliez, qu'ils aillent**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to go to the hospital.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu ailles à l'hôpital.

table.title: aller — subjonctif (irregular)
table.note: Stem all- → aill- in singular & ils; allions/alliez for nous/vous.

cards.english: faire and pouvoir in the subjunctive
cards.word: que je fasse / que je puisse
cards.grammarNote:
**faire** subjunctive: **que je fasse, tu fasses, il fasse, nous fassions, vous fassiez, ils fassent**.
**pouvoir** subjunctive: **que je puisse, tu puisses, il puisse, nous puissions, vous puissiez, ils puissent**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to be able to eat here.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu puisses manger ici.

table.title: faire / pouvoir — subjonctif
table.note: Both have irregular subjunctive stems: fass- and puiss-.

cards.english: douter que + subjunctive (to doubt that)
cards.grammarNote:
Verbs of **doubt** trigger the subjunctive:
**je doute que** (I doubt that), **il n'est pas sûr que** (it's not certain that).
Conversely: **je suis sûr qu'il vient** (I'm sure he's coming) uses the indicative.

contrast.prompt: doubt vs. certainty — subjunctive or indicative?

a.gloss: doubt → subjunctive (vienne)

b.gloss: certainty → indicative (vient)

cards.english: emotions trigger the subjunctive
cards.word: je suis content(e) que tu sois ici
cards.grammarNote:
Expressions of **emotion** (happiness, fear, surprise, sadness) trigger the subjunctive:
**je suis content(e) que** (I'm happy that), **j'ai peur que** (I'm afraid that).
**je suis content que tu sois ici** (I'm happy you're here).
cards.phrase: Je suis content que tu sois ici.

produce.task: say: I'm happy you're here / I'm afraid you're leaving
produce.answer: je suis content que tu sois ici / j'ai peur que tu partes
produce.gloss: Emotion triggers subjunctive. être → sois; partir → partes.

cards.english: venir in the subjunctive
cards.grammarNote:
**venir** subjunctive: **que je vienne, tu viennes, il vienne, nous venions, vous veniez, ils viennent**.
Note the double **n** in most forms: vien**ne**, vien**nes**, vien**nent**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to come to the restaurant.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu viennes au restaurant.

cloze.prompt: I want you to come. (venir → subjunctive, tu form)
cloze.text: je veux que tu ___ au restaurant

cards.english: finir in the subjunctive (regular)
cards.grammarNote:
Regular **-ir** subjunctive: stem from ils/elles present (**finissent → finiss-**) + endings.
**que je finisse, tu finisses, il finisse, nous finissions, vous finissiez, ils finissent**.
cards.englishPhrase: I want you to finish the meal.
cards.phrase: Je veux que tu finisses le repas.

cloze.prompt: I want you to finish the meal. (finir → subjonctif, tu form)
cloze.text: je veux que tu ___ le repas

cards.english: subjunctive trigger summary
cards.word: il faut que / vouloir que / bien que / pour que / avant que
cards.grammarNote:
The most common subjunctive triggers:
**Necessity**: il faut que, il est nécessaire que · **Will/desire**: vouloir que, préférer que · **Emotion**: être content que, avoir peur que · **Concession**: bien que, quoique · **Purpose**: pour que · **Time**: avant que.
cards.englishPhrase: Although you're tired, you must eat.
cards.phrase: Bien que tu sois fatigué, il faut que tu manges.

table.title: Subjunctive triggers (most common)
rows: il faut que, il est nécessaire que
être content que, avoir peur que
table.note: These always trigger subjunctive when the subject of each clause is different.

cards.english: definite articles (the) — le / la / l' / les
cards.word: le pain / la pomme / l'eau / les fruits
cards.grammarNote:
French has four forms of 'the' depending on gender and number:
**le** (masc. sing.), **la** (fem. sing.), **l'** (before vowel/silent h), **les** (plural).
All nouns have gender — learn each noun with its article.
cards.englishPhrase: The bread, the apple, the water, the fruits.
cards.phrase: Le pain, la pomme, l'eau, les fruits.

table.title: Definite articles (the)
table.note: le/la contract to l' before a vowel or silent h.

cards.english: indefinite articles (a/an, some) — un / une / des
cards.word: un café / une pomme / des fruits
cards.grammarNote:
Use **un** (masc.) / **une** (fem.) for 'a / an'; use **des** for 'some' (plural indefinite):
**un café** (a coffee), **une pomme** (an apple), **des fruits** (some fruits).
cards.englishPhrase: I would like a coffee and some fruits.
cards.phrase: Je voudrais un café et des fruits.

table.title: Indefinite articles (a / some)
table.note: des = plural of un/une: a fruit → des fruits.

cards.english: partitive articles (some) — du / de la / de l' / des
cards.word: du pain / de la viande / de l'eau
cards.grammarNote:
Partitives express an unspecified quantity of something (not countable): 'some'.
**du** (de + le, masc.), **de la** (fem.), **de l'** (before vowel), **des** (plural):
**je mange du pain** (I eat some bread), **je bois de l'eau** (I drink some water).
cards.englishPhrase: I am eating some bread and drinking some water.
cards.phrase: Je mange du pain et je bois de l'eau.

table.title: Partitive articles (some — uncountable)
rows: de la (de la viande, de la soupe)
table.note: du = de + le (contraction). Use for foods, substances, abstract nouns.

cards.english: after negation — du/de la/des all become de
cards.word: je ne mange pas de viande
cards.grammarNote:
After **ne … pas**, all articles (un/une, du/de la/des) become **de** (or **d'** before a vowel):
**je mange du pain → je ne mange pas de pain** (I don't eat bread).
**j'ai des fruits → je n'ai pas de fruits** (I don't have any fruit).
cards.phrase: Je ne mange pas de viande.

produce.concept: negation: du/de la/des/un/une → de (d' before vowel)
produce.task: negate: je mange du pain / j'ai des fruits
produce.answer: je ne mange pas de pain / je n'ai pas de fruits
produce.gloss: After ne…pas: all articles collapse to plain de.

cards.english: after quantity expressions — use de, not du/de la
cards.word: beaucoup de pain / un peu de café
cards.grammarNote:
After quantity words, use **de** alone (no article):
**beaucoup de** (a lot of), **un peu de** (a little), **assez de** (enough), **trop de** (too much).
**beaucoup de pain** (a lot of bread) — never *beaucoup du pain*.
cards.englishPhrase: I eat a lot of bread.

cloze.prompt: I eat a lot of bread. (quantity → de alone, not du)

cards.english: definite vs. partitive — in general vs. some of it
cards.word: j'aime le pain / je mange du pain
cards.grammarNote:
Use **definite article** (le/la/les) with verbs of preference (aimer, adorer, préférer) for things in general.
Use **partitive** (du/de la/des) when consuming an unspecified quantity:
**j'aime le café** (I like coffee in general) vs. **je bois du café** (I'm drinking some coffee).
cards.englishPhrase: I like bread. / I eat some bread.
cards.phrase: J'aime le pain. / Je mange du pain.

a.gloss: definite le → like/love in general (always with aimer)

b.gloss: partitive du → some (unspecified quantity of bread)

cards.english: des → de before adjective + noun
cards.grammarNote:
When an adjective comes **before** the noun, **des** becomes **de**:
**des restaurants → de bons restaurants** (some good restaurants).
Exception: fixed phrases like **des jeunes gens** keep des.
cards.englishPhrase: There are some good restaurants here.
cards.phrase: Il y a de bons restaurants ici.

cloze.prompt: There are some good restaurants. (des → de before adjective + noun)
cloze.text: il y a ___ bons restaurants ici

cards.english: no article with professions after être
cards.grammarNote:
After **être**, professions and nationalities take **no article** unless modified:
**je suis médecin** (I'm a doctor), **il est cuisinier** (he's a cook). Add article only with description: **c'est un bon médecin** (he's a good doctor).

a.gloss: no article → plain profession after être

b.gloss: article → with description or identification via c'est

cards.english: I drink some water. (de l'eau — before vowel)
cards.grammarNote:
Before a vowel, the partitive is **de l'** (not *du* or *de la*):
**de l'eau** (some water), **de l'huile** (some oil).
cards.englishPhrase: I drink some water every day.
cards.phrase: Je bois de l'eau tous les jours.

cloze.prompt: I drink some water. (before vowel: de l'...)

cards.english: I don't drink coffee. (du → de after negation)
cards.word: je ne bois pas de café
cards.grammarNote:
**du** becomes plain **de** after negation:
**je bois du café → je ne bois pas de café** (I don't drink coffee).
cards.phrase: Je ne bois pas de café.

cloze.prompt: I don't drink coffee. (du → ? after ne…pas)

cards.english: choosing the right article — review
cards.grammarNote:
Quick decision tree:
- Preference/general? → **le/la/les** (j'aime **le** chocolat)
- Indefinite specific one? → **un/une** (je voudrais **un** café)
- Unspecified quantity? → **du/de la/de l'** (je mange **du** pain)
- After negation/quantity? → plain **de** (je ne mange pas **de** pain)
cards.englishPhrase: I like chocolate. / I want a coffee. / I eat some bread.
cards.phrase: J'aime le chocolat. / Je veux un café. / Je mange du pain.

table.title: Article decision guide
rows: de/d' (pas de pain, beaucoup de pain)
table.note: The definite article with aimer/adorer/préférer is a French signature.

cards.english: I eat a lot of fruits. (beaucoup de — no article)
cards.grammarNote:
After **beaucoup de**, do NOT add an article:
**beaucoup de fruits** (a lot of fruits), **un peu de pain** (a little bread), **trop de sucre** (too much sugar).
cards.englishPhrase: I eat a lot of fruits.

cloze.prompt: I eat a lot of fruits. (quantity: beaucoup ___)

cards.english: un or une? (gender check)
cards.grammarNote:
**un** for masculine nouns, **une** for feminine:
**un restaurant** (m.), **une banque** (f.), **un médecin** (m.), **une pharmacie** (f.).
Always learn nouns with their article to know the gender.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a restaurant and a pharmacy nearby.
cards.phrase: Il y a un restaurant et une pharmacie près d'ici.

produce.concept: un (masc.) vs une (fem.) — agree with noun gender
produce.task: give the article: restaurant / banque / médecin / pharmacie
produce.answer: un restaurant / une banque / un médecin / une pharmacie
produce.gloss: restaurant (m.) → un; banque (f.) → une; médecin (m.) → un; pharmacie (f.) → une.

cards.english: ne … pas — basic negation
cards.grammarNote:
Basic negation wraps the verb: **ne** (before verb) + **pas** (after verb):
**je mange → je ne mange pas** (I don't eat). Before a vowel: **ne → n'**: **je n'ai pas** (I don't have).
cards.phrase: Je ne mange pas de viande.

table.title: ne … pas — basic negation
rows: je ne mange pas de pain
table.note: ne → n' before a vowel. du/de la/des → de after negation.

cards.english: ne … jamais — never
cards.word: je ne mange jamais de viande
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … jamais** = never:
**je ne mange jamais de viande** (I never eat meat). Like **pas**, **jamais** follows the verb in simple tenses, after the auxiliary in compound tenses: **je n'ai jamais mangé de viande**.
cards.phrase: Je ne mange jamais de viande.

cloze.prompt: I never eat meat. (ne … jamais)

cards.english: ne … plus — no more / no longer
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … plus** = no more / no longer / not anymore:
**je ne travaille plus** (I no longer work), **il n'y a plus de pain** (there is no more bread).

cloze.prompt: I no longer work here. (ne … plus)

cards.english: ne … rien — nothing / not anything
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … rien** = nothing / not anything:
**je ne mange rien** (I eat nothing / I'm not eating anything). **rien** can also be a subject: **rien ne va** (nothing is going right).

a.gloss: ne…pas — I don't eat (general negation)

b.gloss: ne…rien — I eat nothing (emphatic: nothing at all)

cards.english: ne … personne — nobody / not anyone
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … personne** = nobody / not anyone:
**je ne vois personne** (I don't see anyone). **personne** can be a subject: **personne ne vient** (nobody is coming).
Note: **personne** ends up after the participle in compound tenses: **je n'ai vu personne**.

cloze.prompt: I don't see anyone. (ne … personne)

cards.english: placement in compound tenses — ne … pas wrap the auxiliary
cards.grammarNote:
In compound tenses (passé composé etc.), **ne … pas/jamais/plus** wrap the **auxiliary** (avoir/être), not the whole verb:
**je n'ai pas mangé** (I didn't eat). Exception: **personne/rien** can come after the participle.

table.title: Negation placement — compound tenses
table.note: pas/jamais/plus/rien: between auxiliary and participle. personne: after participle.

cards.english: ne … ni … ni — neither … nor
cards.word: je ne mange ni viande ni poisson
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … ni … ni** = neither … nor:
**je ne mange ni viande ni poisson** (I eat neither meat nor fish). Articles disappear after **ni**.
cards.englishPhrase: I eat neither meat nor fish.
cards.phrase: Je ne mange ni viande ni poisson.

produce.concept: ne … ni … ni = neither … nor (articles drop after ni)
produce.task: say: I eat neither meat nor fish
produce.answer: je ne mange ni viande ni poisson
produce.gloss: Repeat ni before each element. Articles (du, de la) are dropped.

cards.english: dropping ne in spoken French
cards.word: je sais pas / c'est pas bon
cards.grammarNote:
In everyday spoken French, the **ne** is very often dropped:
**je ne sais pas → je sais pas** (I don't know), **c'est pas bon** (it's not good). The **pas** (or jamais/rien) is enough to signal negation in speech. In writing, keep the **ne**.
cards.phrase: Je ne sais pas. (spoken: je sais pas.)

contrast.prompt: formal written vs. informal spoken negation

a.gloss: formal/written — keep both ne and pas

b.gloss: informal spoken — ne is dropped (very common)

cards.english: I didn't eat the bread. (passé composé negation)
cards.word: je n'ai pas mangé le pain
cards.grammarNote:
In the passé composé, **ne … pas** wrap the auxiliary **avoir/être**:
**je n'ai pas mangé** (I didn't eat). Note: partitive/indefinite articles also become **de**: **je n'ai pas mangé de pain**.
cards.phrase: Je n'ai pas mangé le pain.

cloze.prompt: I didn't eat the bread. (ne…pas around auxiliary in passé composé)

cards.english: ne … que — only (restriction, not negation)
cards.word: je ne mange que du pain
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … que** = only (a restriction, not a true negation):
**je ne mange que du pain** (I eat only bread). Unlike other negators, articles do NOT change to **de** after **que**.
cards.phrase: Je ne mange que du pain.

produce.concept: ne…que = only (article doesn't change to de)
produce.task: say: I eat only bread / I work only here
produce.answer: je ne mange que du pain / je ne travaille que ici
produce.gloss: que comes before the word it restricts. du stays du (not de).

cards.english: I never ate at this restaurant. (ne…jamais in passé composé)
cards.word: je n'ai jamais mangé dans ce restaurant
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … jamais** in the passé composé wraps the auxiliary:
**je n'ai jamais mangé** (I have never eaten). Like **pas**, **jamais** goes between the auxiliary and the participle.
cards.englishPhrase: I have never eaten at this restaurant.
cards.phrase: Je n'ai jamais mangé dans ce restaurant.

cloze.prompt: I have never eaten here. (ne…jamais in passé composé)
cloze.text: je n'ai ___ mangé dans ce restaurant

cards.english: ne … rien vs. ne … personne — thing vs. person
cards.word: je ne vois rien / je ne vois personne
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … rien** = nothing (for things/actions).
**ne … personne** = nobody (for people).
**je ne vois rien** (I see nothing) vs. **je ne vois personne** (I see nobody).
cards.englishPhrase: I see nothing. / I see nobody.
cards.phrase: Je ne vois rien. / Je ne vois personne.

a.gloss: rien = nothing (things/situations)

b.gloss: personne = nobody (people)

cards.english: He no longer works here. (ne…plus)
cards.grammarNote:
**ne … plus** = no longer / not anymore:
**il ne travaille plus ici** (he no longer works here), **je ne mange plus de viande** (I no longer eat meat).

produce.task: say: he no longer works here / I no longer eat meat
produce.answer: il ne travaille plus ici / je ne mange plus de viande
produce.gloss: plus after the verb (present) or auxiliary (compound). de replaces du after.

cards.english: adjective agreement — gender and number
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives agree with the noun they modify in gender and number:
**+e** for feminine, **+s** for plural, **+es** for feminine plural.
**fatigué** (m.) / **fatiguée** (f.) / **fatigués** (m.pl.) / **fatiguées** (f.pl.)

table.title: Adjective agreement — fatigué
table.note: Add -e for fem., -s for pl., -es for fem. pl. If it already ends in -e (triste), form stays the same.

cards.english: adjectives ending in -e — no change for feminine
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives that already end in **-e** do not change for the feminine:
**il est triste → elle est triste** (same form). Only the plural adds **-s**: **ils sont tristes**.
cards.englishPhrase: He is sad. / She is sad.
cards.phrase: Il est triste. / Elle est triste.

cloze.prompt: She is sad. (triste ends in -e → no change for fem.)

cards.english: -eux adjectives → -euse (feminine)
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives ending in **-eux** become **-euse** in the feminine:
**heureux → heureuse** (happy), **nerveux → nerveuse** (nervous), **délicieux → délicieuse**.

cloze.prompt: She is happy. (-eux → -euse for feminine)

cards.english: -er adjectives → -ère (feminine)
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives ending in **-er** become **-ère** in the feminine (accent changes):
**premier → première** (first), **dernier → dernière** (last), **entier → entière** (whole).

table.title: -er → -ère (feminine)
table.note: The -er ending gains an accent grave in the feminine: -ère.

cards.english: adjectives that double the final consonant before -e
cards.grammarNote:
Some adjectives double the final consonant before adding **-e**:
**bon → bonne** (good), **gros → grosse** (big/fat), **gentil → gentille** (nice).

table.title: Consonant-doubling adjectives
table.note: The double consonant keeps the vowel short: bonne /bɔn/ vs. bone would be different.

cards.english: default position — most adjectives follow the noun
cards.grammarNote:
In French, most adjectives come **after** the noun they modify:
**un restaurant délicieux** (a delicious restaurant), **un médecin nerveux** (a nervous doctor).
This is the default. Exception: the BAGS adjectives come before.

a.gloss: most adjectives: AFTER the noun (délicieux follows repas)

b.gloss: BAGS adjectives: BEFORE the noun (bon precedes repas)

cards.english: BAGS adjectives — go before the noun
cards.grammarNote:
**BAGS** adjectives precede the noun — Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size:
**B**eauté: beau, joli · **A**ge: jeune, vieux, nouveau · **G**oodness: bon, mauvais · **S**ize: grand, petit, gros.
**un grand restaurant** (a big restaurant), **un bon repas** (a good meal).

table.title: BAGS adjectives — go BEFORE the noun
table.note: Grand restaurant (size → before). Restaurant délicieux (quality → after).

cards.english: beau / belle / bel — irregular BAGS adjective
cards.grammarNote:
**beau** is irregular before a masculine noun starting with a vowel: **bel**:
**un beau restaurant** (m.) / **un bel hôtel** (m. + vowel) / **une belle vue** (f.) / **de beaux repas** (pl.).

table.title: beau — forms
table.note: bel used before vowel/silent h to avoid clashing vowels.

cards.english: vieux / vieil / vieille — irregular BAGS adjective
cards.grammarNote:
**vieux** (old) has an irregular feminine (**vieille**) and a special form before vowels (**vieil**):
**un vieux restaurant / un vieil hôtel / une vieille maison / de vieux repas**.

cloze.prompt: It's an old hotel. (vieil before vowel/h)

cards.english: adjectives that change meaning by position
cards.word: un grand homme / un homme grand
cards.grammarNote:
A few adjectives change meaning depending on position:
**grand**: **un grand homme** (a great man) vs. **un homme grand** (a tall man).
**ancien**: **un ancien restaurant** (a former restaurant) vs. **un restaurant ancien** (an old restaurant).
cards.englishPhrase: a great man vs. a tall man
cards.phrase: un grand homme / un homme grand

contrast.prompt: grand — before or after the noun?

a.gloss: before = great, important (figurative sense)

b.gloss: after = tall, physically big (literal sense)

cards.english: It's a good meal. (bon — BAGS, before noun, agree)
cards.word: un bon repas / une bonne soupe
cards.grammarNote:
**bon** (good) is a BAGS adjective — it precedes the noun and agrees:
**un bon repas** (m.), **une bonne soupe** (f.), **de bons repas** (m.pl.), **de bonnes soupes** (f.pl.).

cloze.prompt: It's a good soup. (bon → fem. sing.)

cards.english: produce the correct adjective form
cards.grammarNote:
Practice adjective agreement with **nerveux** (nervous), ending **-eux → -euse** (fem.):
**il est nerveux** / **elle est nerveuse** / **ils sont nerveux** / **elles sont nerveuses**.

produce.task: give all four forms of nerveux
produce.answer: nerveux / nerveuse / nerveux / nerveuses
produce.gloss: masc. sg. nerveux, fem. sg. nerveuse, masc. pl. nerveux (no change), fem. pl. nerveuses.

cards.english: It's a bad restaurant. (mauvais — BAGS adjective, before noun)
cards.grammarNote:
**mauvais** (bad) is a BAGS adjective — it precedes the noun:
**un mauvais restaurant** (m.), **une mauvaise soupe** (f.). The feminine adds **-e**: **mauvaise**.

cloze.prompt: It's a bad restaurant. (mauvais — BAGS, before noun)

cards.english: petit vs. grand — size BAGS adjectives
cards.word: un petit café / une grande maison
cards.grammarNote:
**petit** (small) and **grand** (big/great) are BAGS adjectives — they precede the noun and agree:
**un petit café** (m.) / **une petite maison** (f.) / **un grand restaurant** (m.) / **une grande banque** (f.).
cards.englishPhrase: A small coffee and a big house.
cards.phrase: Un petit café et une grande maison.

produce.concept: petit/grand: BAGS adjectives before noun, agree in gender
produce.task: add the adjective: petit (m.) café / grand (f.) maison
produce.answer: un petit café / une grande maison
produce.gloss: petit → fem. petite; grand → fem. grande. Both precede the noun.

cards.english: qui — subject relative pronoun (who / that / which)
cards.grammarNote:
**qui** replaces the **subject** of the relative clause — who/that/which:
**le médecin qui travaille ici** (the doctor who works here). **qui** is never shortened before a vowel.
cards.englishPhrase: The doctor who works here is good.
cards.phrase: Le médecin qui travaille ici est bon.

produce.concept: qui = subject of the relative clause (who/that/which)
produce.task: combine: le médecin + il travaille ici → le médecin qui …
produce.answer: le médecin qui travaille ici
produce.gloss: qui replaces the subject pronoun (il). Verb agrees with the antecedent.

cards.english: que — object relative pronoun (whom / that / which)
cards.grammarNote:
**que** replaces the **direct object** of the relative clause — whom/that/which:
**le repas que je mange** (the meal that I'm eating). **que** becomes **qu'** before a vowel: **le repas qu'il mange**.
cards.englishPhrase: The meal that I'm eating is delicious.
cards.phrase: Le repas que je mange est délicieux.

produce.concept: que = direct object of relative clause (that/which/whom)
produce.task: combine: le repas + je mange le repas → le repas que …
produce.answer: le repas que je mange
produce.gloss: que replaces the object (le repas). que → qu' before vowel.

cards.english: qui vs. que — subject vs. object
cards.word: le médecin qui travaille / le médecin que je vois
cards.grammarNote:
**qui** = the pronoun IS the subject of the clause (does the action).
**que** = the pronoun IS the object (receives the action).
Trick: if a subject follows in the clause → use **que**; if the verb follows directly → use **qui**.
cards.englishPhrase: The doctor who works here. / The doctor that I see.
cards.phrase: Le médecin qui travaille ici. / Le médecin que je vois.

a.gloss: qui = subject (the doctor does the working)

b.gloss: que = object (I see the doctor — je is the subject)

cards.english: dont — replaces de + noun (whose / of which / about which)
cards.grammarNote:
**dont** replaces **de + noun** in the relative clause:
**j'ai besoin du médecin → le médecin dont j'ai besoin** (the doctor that I need — avoir besoin **de**).
Also for possession: **le médecin dont la sœur est infirmière** (the doctor whose sister is a nurse).
cards.englishPhrase: The doctor that I need is here.
cards.phrase: Le médecin dont j'ai besoin est ici.

produce.concept: dont replaces de + noun (needed when verb takes de)
produce.task: combine: le médecin + j'ai besoin du médecin
produce.answer: le médecin dont j'ai besoin
produce.gloss: avoir besoin de → dont absorbs the de. No article needed after dont.

cards.english: où — where / when (place or time)
cards.grammarNote:
**où** refers to **place or time** in relative clauses:
**le restaurant où je mange** (the restaurant where I eat), **le jour où je suis arrivé** (the day when I arrived).
cards.englishPhrase: The restaurant where I eat is nearby.
cards.phrase: Le restaurant où je mange est près d'ici.

cloze.prompt: The restaurant where I eat is nearby. (où for place)
cloze.text: le restaurant ___ je mange est près d'ici

cards.english: The doctor who works at the hospital is kind. (qui = subject)
cards.word: le médecin qui travaille à l'hôpital
cards.grammarNote:
**qui** is used when the relative pronoun is the subject of the clause:
**le médecin qui travaille** (the doctor who works — the doctor does the working).
cards.englishPhrase: The doctor who works at the hospital is kind.
cards.phrase: Le médecin qui travaille à l'hôpital est gentil.

cloze.prompt: The doctor who works at the hospital... (subject → qui)

cards.english: The bread that I eat is fresh. (que = object)
cards.word: le pain que je mange est frais
cards.grammarNote:
**que** is used when the relative pronoun is the **direct object** of the clause:
**le pain que je mange** (the bread that I eat — I am the subject, bread is the object).
cards.englishPhrase: The bread that I eat is fresh.
cards.phrase: Le pain que je mange est frais.

cloze.prompt: The bread that I eat is fresh. (object → que)
cloze.text: le pain ___ je mange est frais

cards.english: dont for possession — whose
cards.word: le médecin dont la sœur est infirmière
cards.grammarNote:
**dont** can express possession (= whose) in relative clauses:
**le médecin dont la sœur est infirmière** (the doctor whose sister is a nurse).
Word order after dont: dont + subject + verb (not dont + verb).
cards.englishPhrase: The doctor whose sister is a nurse is here.
cards.phrase: Le médecin dont la sœur est infirmière est ici.

produce.task: say: the doctor whose sister is a nurse
produce.answer: le médecin dont la sœur est infirmière
produce.gloss: dont + subject + verb. Do not insert de after dont.

cards.english: où for time — the day when
cards.word: le jour où je suis arrivé
cards.grammarNote:
**où** can refer to a point in time as well as place:
**le jour où je suis arrivé** (the day when I arrived), **le moment où je l'ai vu** (the moment when I saw him).
cards.englishPhrase: The day when I arrived was wonderful.
cards.phrase: Le jour où je suis arrivé était merveilleux.

cloze.prompt: The day when I arrived... (où for time)

cards.english: que in passé composé → participle agrees with antecedent
cards.grammarNote:
When the direct object pronoun **que** precedes an **avoir** verb in the passé composé, the participle agrees with the antecedent:
**la soupe que j'ai mangée** (fem. → mangée), **les repas que j'ai mangés** (masc. pl. → mangés).
cards.englishPhrase: The soup that I ate was delicious.
cards.phrase: La soupe que j'ai mangée était délicieuse.

cloze.prompt: The soup that I ate... (que before avoir → participle agrees: fem.)

cards.english: ce qui / ce que — what (without a specific antecedent)
cards.word: ce qui me plaît / ce que je mange
cards.grammarNote:
When there is no specific noun antecedent, use **ce qui** (subject) or **ce que** (object):
**ce qui me plaît** (what pleases me), **ce que je mange** (what I eat).
cards.phrase: Ce que je mange est important.

a.gloss: ce qui = what (subject of the clause: what pleases me)

b.gloss: ce que = what (object of the clause: what I eat)

cards.english: dont vs. où — de + noun vs. place/time
cards.word: le restaurant dont je parle / le restaurant où je mange
cards.grammarNote:
**dont** replaces **de + noun**: **je parle du restaurant → le restaurant dont je parle**.
**où** replaces a place complement: **je mange dans le restaurant → le restaurant où je mange**.
cards.englishPhrase: The restaurant I'm talking about. / The restaurant where I eat.
cards.phrase: Le restaurant dont je parle. / Le restaurant où je mange.

a.gloss: dont → replaces de (parler de)

b.gloss: où → replaces dans/à (place)

cards.english: use all four relative pronouns in context
cards.grammarNote:
Summary of the four main relative pronouns:
**qui** = subject (who/that), **que** = object (that/which), **dont** = de + noun (whose/of which), **où** = place/time (where/when).
cards.englishPhrase: The restaurant where I eat, which I love, and which my friend talks about.
cards.phrase: Le restaurant où je mange, que j'aime, et dont mon ami parle.
